content.text:
I built `/work/index.html`: a linked overview-and-detail chart in D3 that loads all 263,088 rows straight from the URL. It renders with no errors or warnings. I rendered it at three zoom levels (3 days, about 80 days, about 5 hours), and all three look correct. The brush and zoom are only tested in the code, not by clicking through them.

**How it works**
- **Overview:** the whole of 2020–2024. A shaded band shows each day's lowest and highest temperature, and a line shows the daily mean. Drag across it (the brush) to pick the period for the detail view.
- **Detail:** temperature on top, rain bars below it on the same time axis. You can also scroll and drag inside it, and the overview selection follows. At any zoom it picks the finest bin size that fits the width: 10 min, 30 min, 1 h, 3 h, 6 h, 12 h, 1 day or 7 days.
- **Down to single readings:** at the 10-minute level it draws the raw readings, and each one gets a dot once there are few enough points. Hovering shows the exact reading.
- **Caption:** every figure in it is computed when the page loads:
  - Monthly means range from 1.5 °C (January 2020) to 24.1 °C (August 2024).
  - The typical day-night swing is 8.6 °C.
  - 4.2% of 10-minute intervals are wet.
  - The peak is 26.7 mm in 10 minutes, at 2024-08-17 14:40 UTC.
- **Start view:** the 3 days around that rain peak, which is also computed from the data.

```
REPORT
deliverable: index.html
requirements:
  R1: done - daily min–max band + daily mean of tl for 2020–2024, computed in the page
  R2: done - detail shows raw 10-min readings (with dots) when zoomed in; 30 min–7 day bins when zoomed out
  R3: done - brush in overview sets the detail period; zoom/pan in detail moves the brush back
  R4: done - rr bar track below tl, same time axis
  R5: done - overview: months + years; detail: months/days down to HH:MM, chosen by zoom level
  R6: done - all 263,088 rows fetched and parsed; aggregation happens in the page
  R7: done - axes labelled °C, mm per 10 min (or per bin), Time (UTC); title + computed caption
assumptions:
  - Empty fields would be treated as missing (NaN); none exist in this file (0 missing tl, 0 rr)
  - When zoomed out, rr is shown as the sum per bin and the axis label changes to "mm per <bin>"
  - Each 10-min bar is centred on its timestamp; the interval convention was not checked
  - Start view is 3 days around the wettest 10-min interval, found from the data
  - Bins are aligned to UTC epoch (whole days/hours)
limitations:
  - At the full 5-year detail zoom, bins are 7 days, so short events show only as min/max/sum
  - A 3-day selection is only about 2 px wide in the overview (outlined to stay visible)
  - Zooming in stops at about 2 hours across
```
